Red Wing, the legacy footwear brand setting the global standard for purpose-built boots since 1905, just released the new Construct boots, designed to withstand even the harshest work sites.

# Inside the Making of Red Wing’s New Comfort-Focused Work Boot Line
The Construct collection is launching for fall 2026.

[Red Wing](https://wwd.com/tag/red-wing/) is bringing sneaker-esque [comfort](https://wwd.com/tag/comfort/) to [work boots](https://wwd.com/tag/work-boots/) with a new collection launching for fall 2026.
The Construct line, consisting of three boot styles, prioritizes [comfort](https://wwd.com/footwear-news/shoe-industry-news/joor-luxury-global-footwear-price-sandals-flats-sneakers-1238352476/), fit and durability while also offering the same essential safety features, high-level performance and refined aesthetic typical of [Red Wing](https://wwd.com/footwear-news/shoe-industry-news/american-shoe-factories-new-balance-red-wing-1239032392/) products.
“From the outside, it looks like a really nice classic leather brown boot, but we wanted to pack it full of technology and comfort features,” said Ryan Merkt, director of merchandising, direct-to-consumer and industrial at Red Wing.

Other elements of the Construct boots include a cushioned tongue and lace-to-toe construction, plus a drop-down at the heel, to provide more flexibility for workers who do a lot of bending down on the job.

The line comprises a 6-inch soft-toe boot retailing for $270 and a safety-toe version priced at $280, while an 8-inch safety-toe boot will sell for $290.
Construct is set to replace the DynaForce line, which was introduced more than a decade ago and whose styles will be gradually discontinued. Merkt said that in recent years, there have been updates to ASTM certifications and regulatory requirements, particularly around slip-resistance. “So we really wanted to build a new boot family that exceeded those new slip-resistant requirements and was best in class there, while also upping the comfort factor,” he said.

Red Wing Shoes is bringing sneaker-esque comfort to work boots with a new collection launching for fall 2026.

The Construct line, consisting of three boot styles, prioritizes comfort, fit and durability while also offering the same essential safety features, high-level performance and refined aesthetic typical of Red Wing products.

“From the outside, it looks like a really nice classic leather brown boot, but we wanted to pack it full of technology and comfort features,” said Ryan Merkt, director of merchandising, direct-to-consumer and industrial at Red Wing.

He noted that expectations for work boots have changed, where customers are looking for their work gear to be as comfortable as their casual wear. “It is highly important for that next generation of consumers,” Merkt said. “I think that is first and foremost on their mind.” And even core Red Wing customers are shifting toward existing products that feature more out-of-the-box comfort, he added.

Merkt joked that breaking in a classic Red Wing work boot is considered a rite of passage for some tradespeople. But the Construct collection offers something different.

The Construct line includes three styles: a 6-inch boot that comes in a safety-toe and soft-toe version, and an 8-inch safety-toe boot. Courtesy of Red Wing Shoes

First, the outsole has a dual-density construction, whereby a rubber cupsole is filled with a lighter-density polyurethane. “It gives you nice underfoot cushion, and with that welt construction, it softens it up and helps with the break-in period,” said Merkt.

He noted that Red Wing has used a similar construction in other boot families, and it has proven its worth. “It stands up to a lot of different things: great heat resistance, chemical resistance and oil-and-gas resistance, as well as being super abrasion resistant and offering probably our best slip resistance, both in wet and oily environments.”

seltz.title: Red Wing Traveled to the World’s Northernmost Inhabited Town to Test Out Its Newest Boot
seltz.snippet:
Red Wing Heritage is getting ready for the colder months with its newest launch.

On Thursday, the Minnesota-based footwear brand unveiled the new Norway Moc, a boot “built for life in cold climates and designed to meet the demands of northern winters,” the company noted.

Built on Red Wing’s signature moc toe silhouette, the new made-in-America Norway Moc features a Scotch-grain embossed Copper Rough and Tough leather that delivers four times more water resistance, while a Vibram Fire and Ice Lug outsole provides traction and comfort in cold, challenging conditions. A breathable lining and padded collar help regulate warmth and moisture, while a removable felt-covered footbed adds comfort throughout the day.

And despite its name, Amy Peck, vice president of product innovation at Red Wing, said in a statement that the new silhouette “isn’t a Scandinavian-inspired boot.”

The Red Wing Heritage Norway Moc. Courtesy of Red Wing Heritage

“It’s a Minnesotan boot built for Norwegian winters,” Peck noted. “It’s designed for the realities of life in cold climates and built by people who understand what winter demands.”

To bring the launch to life, the footwear brand tapped acclaimed filmmaker Benjamin Hardman on a film that follows a pair of Norway Mocs on an expedition from Red Wing, Minn., across sweeping arctic tundras to a remote cabin in Svalbard, Norway, which is home to Longyearbyen, the world’s northernmost permanently inhabited town.

The Norway Moc, which retails for $369.99, is now available at Redwingshoes.com, in Red Wing stores and at select retailers.

# Inside the Making of Red Wing’s New Comfort-Focused Work Boot Line
The Construct collection is launching for fall 2026.

[Red Wing](https://wwd.com/tag/red-wing/) is bringing sneaker-esque [comfort](https://wwd.com/tag/comfort/) to [work boots](https://wwd.com/tag/work-boots/) with a new collection launching for fall 2026.
The Construct line, consisting of three boot styles, prioritizes [comfort](https://wwd.com/footwear-news/shoe-industry-news/joor-luxury-global-footwear-price-sandals-flats-sneakers-1238352476/), fit and durability while also offering the same essential safety features, high-level performance and refined aesthetic typical of [Red Wing](https://wwd.com/footwear-news/shoe-industry-news/american-shoe-factories-new-balance-red-wing-1239032392/) products.
“From the outside, it looks like a really nice classic leather brown boot, but we wanted to pack it full of technology and comfort features,” said Ryan Merkt, director of merchandising, direct-to-consumer and industrial at Red Wing.

Other elements of the Construct boots include a cushioned tongue and lace-to-toe construction, plus a drop-down at the heel, to provide more flexibility for workers who do a lot of bending down on the job.

The line comprises a 6-inch soft-toe boot retailing for $270 and a safety-toe version priced at $280, while an 8-inch safety-toe boot will sell for $290.
Construct is set to replace the DynaForce line, which was introduced more than a decade ago and whose styles will be gradually discontinued. Merkt said that in recent years, there have been updates to ASTM certifications and regulatory requirements, particularly around slip-resistance. “So we really wanted to build a new boot family that exceeded those new slip-resistant requirements and was best in class there, while also upping the comfort factor,” he said.
